question:
You are given the following system of equations:

$2x + y - z = 3$

$x - y + 2z = -1$

$3x + 2y + z = 4$

(a) Represent the system in matrix form.
(b) Using the inverse of the coefficient matrix, solve for $x$, $y$, $z$. Include calculations for minors, cofactors, adjoint, inverse, and all intermediate steps.
explanation:
Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$, $X = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix}$, $B = \begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -1 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}$.

$AX = B$

Step 1: $|A| = 2\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{vmatrix} - 1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{vmatrix} + (-1)\begin{vmatrix}1 & -1 \\ 3 & 2\end{vmatrix}$

$= 2((-1)(1) - (2)(2)) - ((1)(1)-(2)(3)) - (1)((1)(2)-(-1)(3))$

$= 2(-1-4) - (1-6) - (1)(2+3)$

$= 2(-5) - (-5) - 5$

$= -10 + 5 - 5 = -10$

$|A| = -10 \neq 0$; unique solution exists.

Step 2: Find minors and cofactors.

Row 1:
$M_{11} = \begin{vmatrix}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{vmatrix} = -1-4 = -5$, $C_{11} = -5$
$M_{12} = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{vmatrix} = 1-6=-5$, $C_{12} = +5$
$M_{13} = \begin{vmatrix}1 & -1 \\ 3 & 2\end{vmatrix} = 2+3=5$, $C_{13} = +5$

Row 2:
$M_{21} = \begin{vmatrix}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{vmatrix} = 1+2=3$, $C_{21} = -3$
$M_{22} = \begin{vmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{vmatrix} = 2-(-3)=5$, $C_{22}=5$
$M_{23} = \begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{vmatrix} = 4-3=1$, $C_{23} = -1$

Row 3:
$M_{31} = \begin{vmatrix}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{vmatrix}=2-1=1$, $C_{31} = +1$
$M_{32}=\begin{vmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{vmatrix}=4+1=5$, $C_{32}=-5$
$M_{33}=\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{vmatrix}=-2-1=-3$, $C_{33}=-3$

Cofactor matrix:
$\begin{bmatrix} -5 & 5 & 5 \\ -3 & 5 & -1 \\ 1 & -5 & -3 \end{bmatrix}$

adj $A = $ transpose of cofactor matrix:
$\begin{bmatrix} -5 & -3 & 1 \\ 5 & 5 & -5 \\ 5 & -1 & -3 \end{bmatrix}$

$A^{-1} = \frac{1}{|A|}\text{adj }A = -\frac{1}{10}\begin{bmatrix}-5 & -3 & 1 \\ 5 & 5 & -5 \\ 5 & -1 & -3 \end{bmatrix}$

Step 3: $X = A^{-1}B$:

$A^{-1}B = -\frac{1}{10} \begin{bmatrix}-5 & -3 & 1 \\ 5 & 5 & -5 \\ 5 & -1 & -3 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -1 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}$

Row 1: $-5*3 + (-3)*(-1) + 1*4 = -15 + 3 + 4 = -8$
Row 2: $5*3 + 5*(-1) + (-5)*4 = 15 - 5 - 20 = -10$
Row 3: $5*3 + (-1)*(-1) + (-3)*4 = 15 + 1 - 12 = 4$

So vector: $\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -10 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}$

Multiply by $-\frac{1}{10}$ to get:

$x = \frac{8}{10} = 0.8$
$y = 1$
$z = -0.4$

Final solution: $x = 0.8,\ y = 1,\ z = -0.4$

options.A:
(a) $AX=B$, where $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1&-1\\1&-1&2\\3&2&1\end{bmatrix}$, $X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}$, $B=\begin{bmatrix}3\\-1\\4\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) $|A|=0$, so the inverse does not exist and the system has no unique solution.
options.B:
(a) $AX=B$, where $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1&-1\\1&-1&2\\3&2&1\end{bmatrix}$, $X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}$, $B=\begin{bmatrix}3\\-1\\4\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) $|A|=-10\ne0$, so $A^{-1}$ exists and the solution is $x=0.8,\ y=1,\ z=-0.4$.
options.C:
(a) $AX=B$, where $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1&-1\\1&-1&2\\3&2&1\end{bmatrix}$, $X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}$, $B=\begin{bmatrix}3\\-1\\4\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) $|A|=10\ne0$, so $A^{-1}$ exists and the solution is $x=-0.8,\ y=-1,\ z=0.4$.
options.D:
(a) $AX=B$, where $A=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1&4\\2&1&-1\\1&-1&2\end{bmatrix}$, $X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}$, $B=\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\\3\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) $|A|=-10\ne0$, so the solution is $x=1,\ y=0.8,\ z=-0.4$.
